study_identification_part.si4_title: Neuroanatomical heterogeneity and homogeneity in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify neuroanatomical heterogeneity in structural magnetic resonance imaging measures (cortical surface area, cortical thickness, subcortical volume, and intracranial volume) in individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P) compared with healthy controls (HC), and in relation to subsequent transition to a first episode of psychosis.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: The study used two main approaches to quantify deviation/heterogeneity: 1) Group-level metrics: Variability Ratio (VR) and Coefficient of Variation (CV) ratio to compare inter-individual variability between groups. 2) Personalized metric: Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) to quantify how similar an individual's brain profile is to others in their group (within-group) or to the healthy control group (normative). Deviations in the normative PBSI were defined as z-scores > 1.5 SD from the HC mean.
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The statistical analysis section clearly details the different metrics used to assess heterogeneity and deviation from the norm.

Personalised estimates of heterogeneity of SA, CT and SV brain pro /uniFB01 les were indexed with the novel Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI)... We set >1.5 SD as a threshold to identify individuals at CHR-P who most markedly deviated from the normative neuroanatomical pro /uniFB01 le, in line with previous work [37].

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons (CHR-P vs HC; CHR-T vs CHR-NT) of VR, CV ratio, and PBSI scores were conducted using t-tests. Multivariable regression models, adjusting for age and sex, were used to investigate the effects of transition status, subgroup status, antipsychotic exposure, and psychopathology severity on PBSI scores. P-values were corrected for multiple comparisons using the False Discovery Rate (FDR).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: While no significant regional neuroanatomical heterogeneity was found after FDR correction, personalized analyses revealed greater divergence in global brain profiles (surface area, cortical thickness, subcortical volume) in CHR-P individuals compared to controls, though this was not associated with transition to psychosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found no significant regional heterogeneity in CHR-P individuals compared to healthy controls after FDR correction, using Variability Ratio (VR) and Coefficient of Variation (CV) ratio. However, the Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) revealed significantly greater neuroanatomical divergence (lower similarity) in global surface area (p < 0.01), cortical thickness (p < 0.01), and subcortical volume (p < 0.01) profiles in the CHR-P group. A normative PBSI analysis identified a small subset of CHR-P individuals with marked deviation from the healthy control profile in surface area (0.70%), cortical thickness (7.47%), and subcortical volume (10.20%). None of the heterogeneity or divergence metrics were significantly associated with subsequent transition to psychosis.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: 1. The validity of different heterogeneity indices (VR vs PBSI) is debated, and they produced conceptually discrepant findings. 2. Inability to control for confounding factors like substance use. 3. The dichotomous outcome of transition vs. no transition may not capture the full range of clinical outcomes. 4. Substantial variation in follow-up duration between sites may have reduced power to detect differences related to transition.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, the validity of the VR as an index of heterogeneity has been debated... Second, we were also unable to control for further potentially confounding factors, such as substance use... The lack of an association between heterogeneity and transition to psychosis may re/uniFB02 ect the challenges we face when employing dichotomous diagnostic criteria... Furthermore, there was substantial variation in follow-up duration between sites. As such, it is possible that the presence of individuals at CHR-P that were classi/uniFB01 ed as ' no transition '-yet who may have developed psychosis following their /uniFB01 nal data contributions -may have reduced our power to detect group differences.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study introduced a novel application of the Person-Based Similarity Index (PBSI) in a large-scale CHR-P cohort, using it for both within-group similarity assessment and normative modeling to identify individuals with deviant brain profiles. This highlights a move towards personalized, individual-level metrics over traditional group-average comparisons.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study is notable for being the largest pooled neuroimaging study of CHR-P individuals to date. A key finding is the discrepancy between regional (VR/CV ratio) and global, personalized (PBSI) measures of heterogeneity. While regional differences were not significant, the personalized approach revealed significant divergence, suggesting that heterogeneity in CHR-P might be better captured by global, multi-region patterns rather than isolated regional effects. The study also highlights that a relatively small percentage of the CHR-P population shows marked neuroanatomical deviation.
